goal.title: Telemetry export foundation
criteria: With all three export settings well-formed, sending is on, and the status text names the Grafana host and never the token.
With the settings unset, the status says sending is off. With some missing or malformed, it says sending is off and which setting is wrong, without echoing the token. Neither case is an error.
Against a receiver that is unreachable, hangs or rejects, handing over data returns immediately, and queued data stays bounded (oldest or newest dropped, never unbounded growth).

Failure warnings appear only after five minutes of continuous failure, at most once per five minutes, stop after a successful send, and never contain the token, the Basic header value or raw error text.
Shutdown flushes for no more than two seconds.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/observe/settings.go:189 (diff line 1293) builds "telemetry export: on (Grafana Cloud " + ex.host + ")" when export() reports on. ex.host is the URL host from httpsBase (settings.go:~99-105 via url.Parse, userinfo rejected). The token is never placed in the string, and the status test in settings_test.go:43-70 ('all set') asserts the exact text and checks Token is absent from both status strings.

Unset: settings.go:193-195 returns "telemetry export: off (no TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_* settings)" with no error value (Status returns only strings). Missing or malformed: settings.go:191 returns "warning: telemetry export: off (<problems>)", where problems (export(), settings.go:115-145) name only the setting, e.g. 'TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_INSTANCE_ID is not a number', 'TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_TOKEN contains spaces', 'TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_OTLP_URL is not an https URL'. No problem string includes a setting value. settings_test.go:43-100 covers these cases and checks the token is absent.

observe.go:33-38 sets queueSize=2048. Traces and logs go to SDK batch processors with WithMaxQueueSize(queueSize) (observe.go:136-144); the SDK batchers enqueue without blocking and drop when full, so the newest data is dropped and memory is bounded. Metrics go through a periodic reader, which holds only aggregated series. Exporter retry is disabled and each client has a 5s timeout (observe.go:~100-120). Start (observe.go:66) returns without any network call. Tests: observe_test.go:~39-75 TestHandingOverNeverWaits runs 5000 hand-overs against unreachable, hanging and rejecting receivers with per-call and total time ceilings. observe_test.go:~128-140 TestQueuedDataStaysBounded runs 40,000 padded spans and records against a hanging receiver and bounds heap growth at 96 MB.

health.go:43-46 defines failAfter=5m, warnEvery=5m, healthEvery=30s. note() (health.go:60-73) sets failingSince on the first failure and clears it on success, so only unbroken failure counts. check() (health.go:86-113) warns only when a signal has failed for at least failAfter, gates repeats by lastWarn at warnEvery, and resets lastWarn when nothing is failing, which stops warnings after a success. The line (health.go:117-118) names only signal names and a kind from kind() (health.go:137-152: timeout, unreachable, rejected (HTTP n), failed). It never includes err.Error(), the token or the Basic value. Tests: health_test.go:43-70 (timing and 5m-to-5m cadence, and asserts absence of token, Basic value, 'Unauthorized' and 'body:'), health_test.go:~80-93 (stops after a success), health_test.go:~96-103 (continuous failure only), health_test.go:~138-156 (real exporters against a 401 receiver).

observe.go:33-38 sets shutdownWithin=2s. Shutdown (observe.go:188-208) wraps the caller's context in a 2s timeout, runs the tracer, logger and meter Shutdown in parallel goroutines writing to a buffered channel, and returns ctx.Err() as soon as the deadline fires. The caller's context cannot extend it. Test observe_test.go:~140-148 TestShutdownFlushesForAtMostTwoSeconds asserts a hanging receiver shuts down within 2.5s. Shutdown still flushes queued data when the receiver answers (TestShutdownFlushesQueuedData).

items.title: Records and log lines sent to Grafana

goal.title: Records and log lines sent to Grafana
criteria: In a hosted session against a fake receiver, every record printed to standard output arrives as a log record with the identical line as its body. The start-up line, card-set lines and warnings arrive too.
Standard output and standard error are unchanged by turning sending on, so the live log view looks as before.
Sign-in records carry `"provider":"google"`, and the record catalogue in the runbook lists the field.
With the receiver unreachable, hanging or rejecting, a player can sign in, import a game and play, with no added wait.
The start-up line says whether sending is on, off or incomplete, and never shows the token.
The desktop playmat, run with the Grafana settings present and used, makes no connection to the receiver.
The app definition declares the new settings with the token as a secret with no value, and the image's settings note lists them.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: Records are forwarded via recordSink (internal/observe/sink.go:57-80) and the sink is set in runHosted (cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:502), but some warnings never reach the log writer. (a) hosted.go:63 'warning: no public URL set' is printed by hostedPublicURL, which runHosted calls at hosted.go:485, before hostedTelemetry (hosted.go:490) installs log.SetOutput. (b) main.go:195-196 envInt warnings (hosted.go:91, 'is not a whole number') fire during flag setup, before runHosted. (c) hosted.go:464-466 writes the telemetry 'warning: ...' status line with log.Print before log.SetOutput at hosted.go:467-469, so that warning is not sent. The criterion says warnings arrive too; the test (hosted_telemetry_test.go:399) only checks a warning the test writes itself, so it does not cover these cases.

Log output is teed rather than replaced: hosted.go:467-469 uses io.MultiWriter(log.Writer(), tel.LogWriter()), so stderr still gets every line. Record output still goes only to the recorder writer (internal/telemetry/recorder.go RecordContext, r.w.Write unchanged) and the sink is called after the write. Off-vs-on comparison is in hosted_telemetry_test.go:463-485. The only stderr difference is the start-up line's export text, which criterion 5 requires.

internal/hostauth/google.go:233 records telemetry.SignIn with Provider: "google"; internal/telemetry/recorder.go adds the provider JSON field (lines 71-76 and 'Provider: e.Provider'). docs/observability.md:692 lists `provider` in the field table, :701 shows it on the sign_in example, and :710 names it on the sign_in row.

The record sink and log writer only call non-blocking OTel logger Emit (sink.go:57-80, logwriter.go emit), and the batch processors queue with a size cap of 2048 (observe.go:1416-1525). Exporters use a 5s timeout with retries disabled (observe.go:1473-1480). Shutdown is capped at 2s (observe.go:1573). Tests TestHostedPlaysOnWhenGrafanaFails (hosted_telemetry_test.go:491-520) and TestHandingOverNeverWaits (observe_test.go:1705-1736) cover unreachable, hanging and rejecting receivers.

Settings.Status (internal/observe/settings.go:2194-2214) returns 'telemetry export: on (Grafana Cloud <host>)', 'telemetry export: off (no TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_* settings)', or 'warning: telemetry export: off (<missing or bad settings>)'. hosted.go:320 appends exportText to the start-up line. The token is never formatted: only setting names and the host appear, and httpsBase rejects userinfo. The word 'incomplete' is not used; the warning form with named missing settings stands in for it. The 'warning:' line itself is not sent, see criterion 1.

Only cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go, hosted_test.go, main.go (config type and Settings only) and test files import internal/observe; a grep of the code root shows no desktop package importing it. observe.Start is called only from hosted.go:468. TestOnlyHostedStartsTelemetry (desktop_telemetry_test.go:220-253) enforces this, and TestDesktopSendsNothing (desktop_telemetry_test.go:143-215) asserts zero requests to the receiver.

The diff adds .do/app.yaml keys TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_OTLP_URL, _INSTANCE_ID, _METRICS_URL and _METRICS_USER with scope RUN_TIME and no value, and TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_TOKEN with type: SECRET and no value (app.yaml hunk, diff lines 9-30). Dockerfile diff lines 43-48 adds the same settings to the image's settings note.

verdicts.evidence: Records: internal/telemetry/recorder.go RecordContext writes r.w.Write(b) then calls sink.Emit with JSON: b (the exact written line); internal/observe/sink.go:Emit sets body to bytes.TrimRight(l.JSON, "\n"). The recorder writes to os.Stdout by default (cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:150-154). The sink is attached in runHosted at hosted.go:506, before loader.Start and the listener, so the startup line (hosted.go:523), card-set lines and warnings go through the log writer. Log lines: hosted.go:287-288 replays c.earlyLog and adds tel.LogWriter() to log output; internal/observe/logwriter.go emits each line with the std date prefix stripped, WARN for 'warning:' lines. Covered by TestHostedRecordsAndLogLinesReachGrafana and TestMainHostedSendsStartupLines in cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_telemetry_test.go (I did not run them; judged from code).

Stdout: recorder writes the same bytes to the same writer whether or not a sink is set (recorder.go RecordContext, the sink is called after r.w.Write, outside the lock). Stderr: main.go:719 log output is io.MultiWriter(os.Stderr, &early) and hosted.go:288 only adds a writer beside log.Writer(), so stderr still receives every line. TestHostedOutputUnchangedBySending compares records and log lines with sending on and off. Caveat, not a failure: the start-up line's export clause necessarily differs (criterion 5 requires it), and the 'warning: telemetry export: sending ... has failed' line appears only after five minutes of failed sending (observe/health.go:1018-1052).

internal/hostauth/google.go:233 records telemetry.Event{Name: SignIn, Email: acct.Email, Provider: "google"}; internal/telemetry/recorder.go line struct has Provider `json:"provider,omitempty"` and Record copies e.Provider into it. docs/observability.md:741 adds the field row '| `provider` | the sign-in provider (`google`), on `sign_in` |' to the record catalogue, and line 757 lists provider in the sign_in event row. Example line at 748 shows "provider":"google".

The sink and log writer only enqueue: observe/sink.go Emit and observe/logwriter.go emit call the SDK logger, whose batch processors drop when the queue is full (queueSize 2048, observe/observe.go:1459-1466, 1563-1572). Exporters use a 5s timeout with retry disabled (observe/observe.go:1523-1546, 1527/1535/1543). The recorder calls the sink outside its lock (recorder.go). Hosted wiring sets up telemetry before serving (hosted.go:482-484). TestHostedPlaysOnWhenGrafanaFails (hosted_telemetry_test.go) times a session against unreachable, hanging and rejecting receivers versus sending off, allowing one second. Judged from code; the test was not run by me.

observe/settings.go:2241-2261 Status returns 'telemetry export: on (Grafana Cloud <host>)', 'warning: telemetry export: off (incomplete: ...)' or 'telemetry export: off (no TCGREPLAY_* settings)'. hosted.go:290-296 passes it through, and hosted.go:523 puts it on the start-up line. The problem strings name only setting names (settings.go:2174-2197), and the health line and errors avoid error text (health.go:1070-1085). The token is never formatted anywhere in the diff.

The observe package is imported only by hosted.go (which calls observe.Start from runHosted and the hosted helper) and by main.go, which uses only the observe.Settings type in config (main.go diff: config.telemetry field). cmd/tcgreplay/desktop_telemetry_test.go TestDesktopSendsNothing exercises in-process and daemon desktop use with all settings set and asserts zero receiver requests; TestOnlyHostedStartsTelemetry AST-checks that only hosted.go calls observe functions. Judged from code and test source; the tests were not run by me.

.do/app.yaml diff lines 9-30 declare TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_OTLP_URL, TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_INSTANCE_ID, TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_METRICS_URL and TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_METRICS_USER as RUN_TIME with no value, and TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_TOKEN as RUN_TIME SECRET with no value. Dockerfile diff lines 42-48 add a settings note listing all five settings in the image's comment block. Caveat: Dockerfile is not in the scope list, but criterion 7 requires the note there.

items.title: Every HTTP request and outside call traced

goal.title: Every HTTP request and outside call traced
criteria: Every request to the hosted playmat (website, board page, card data, live connection, sign-in steps, MCP, admin) produces a server span named by its route.
A request carrying a W3C `traceparent`, sampled or not, produces spans in that trace, parented on the incoming span.
The Google token exchange appears as a timed part inside the sign-in callback's trace. Card set fetches, image store calls and CDN purges appear as client spans.
No span leaving the playmat carries a client address, user agent, query string, Google authorization code, OAuth state or board handle.
The live connection and MCP streams still work through the wrapper (websocket upgrade and streaming are not broken).
No per-route HTTP metrics are sent.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: hosted.go hostedServeHandler (around line 380) wraps the whole hosted handler (movedGuard + hostedHandler) in tel.Handler, and runHosted serves through it (line 419). http.go Handler uses otelhttp with serverSpanName, so the span is named 'METHOD route' from r.Pattern, with http.route set by routeNamer. hostedHandler (cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go ~261-283) covers /board, /assets/, /ws, /api/, /mcp, /admin, / and the sign-in routes via a.Routes. TestHostedTracesEveryRequest (hosted_trace_test.go:44-90) asserts a named server span and http.route for GET /, /board, /api/, /ws, /auth/login, /auth/google/callback, /authorize, POST /token, /register, /mcp, /admin.

http.go Handler sets otelhttp.WithPropagators(propagation.TraceContext{}) and WithPublicEndpointFn(false) so the incoming context is the parent, not a link, and the sampler is AlwaysSample (observe.go sdktrace setup; test helper traced() in http_test.go:2001). TestHandlerJoinsIncomingTrace (http_test.go:2061) checks flags 00 and 01 give a span in the incoming trace with the incoming span as parent and no links. TestHostedJoinsIncomingTrace (hosted_trace_test.go:164) covers the hosted path.

Google token exchange: hosted.go hostedAuth passes HTTPClient: tel.Client(nil) (~line 287) into hostauth.Config; hostauth.go:116 stores it as a.client; google.go:121 puts it in the exchange context and google.go:122 calls a.google.Exchange with the request-derived ctx. TestHostedSignInTraceHoldsTheGoogleCall (hosted_trace_test.go:94-121) asserts a client span 'POST <token host>' whose TraceID and Parent equal the callback server span. Card set fetch: loader.HTTP = tel.Client(loader.HTTP) (hosted.go ~402), and TestHostedAdminCheckTracesTheCardSetFetch (hosted_trace_test.go:126-159) asserts a client span in the check's trace. Image store and CDN purge: hosted.go hostedImages wraps cfg.HTTP, images.HTTP and cdn.HTTP (lines ~407-425); TestHostedImageClientsTraced (hosted_trace_test.go:227) covers the purge as a client span. The fields exist in internal/spaces/config.go:33, internal/spaces/cdn.go:37, internal/cards/images.go:83 and internal/catalog/loader.go:69.

filter.go: allowedAttrs (lines 1407-1418) holds only method, route, status code, url.scheme, url.path, url.full, server.address, server.port, network.protocol.version and error.type. Everything else is dropped, including client.address, network.peer.*, user_agent.original, url.query and http.target. url.full has its query and fragment cut by stripQuery (1472-1477). Status descriptions and events are scrubbed (1467, 1462-1466): only tcgreplay.* events pass, so exception events carrying the code are dropped. Span names come from route patterns, not raw paths. The only board handle is in the ?board= query, which is stripped. TestFilterKeepsOnlyAllowedAttributes (http_test.go:2088) and TestHostedSpansCarryNothingIdentifying (hosted_trace_test.go:190-212) check the markers HANDLEMARKER, AGENTMARKER, code=, state=, board=. No app code sets tcgreplay.* attributes (grep of non-test internal code shows only http.route).

http.go wraps with otelhttp.NewHandler, which passes the ResponseWriter through and does not buffer. http_test.go:2148 TestHandlerKeepsWebsocketAndStreaming dials a websocket through the wrapper and echoes a message, and checks that an MCP-style text/event-stream flush reaches the client. runHosted's http.Server keeps no WriteTimeout (hosted.go ~417). I did not run the tests myself; the verify step reports them passing.

http.go:904 and :967 pass otelhttp.WithMeterProvider(metricnoop.NewMeterProvider()) to both the server handler and the client transport, so otelhttp emits no HTTP metrics. The doc comment on Handler (http.go:15-19) states this. No other otelhttp instance was found in the diff. I did not find a per-route metric in observe.go or hosted.go.

items.title: Tool calls and board actions traced with records linked to their trace

goal.title: Tool calls and board actions traced with records linked to their trace
criteria: Each tool call has a span naming the tool, the assistant and the player ID, inside the trace of its own MCP request. Two calls on one session land in two traces.
Calls refused by the rate limit are traced too, and their `limited` record carries the trace.
Each board action has its own span naming the action, linked to the live connection's span.
The error record of a failed import carries the trace and span IDs of that tool call's span, and the span is marked failed with the same redacted message.

Sign-in, sign-out, refusal, limit, board refusal and admin records carry the trace of the request that caused them. Background records (idle games, idle accounts) carry none and are otherwise unchanged.
The desktop board works exactly as before.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/observe/mcp.go:31-90 makes each tools/call a span "tools/call <tool>" with tcgreplay.tool, tcgreplay.assistant and tcgreplay.player, extracting the parent from the request headers (Extra.Header) rather than the stale session context. CarryContext (mcp.go:23-35) writes each HTTP request's own span into those headers, and cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:302-308 wires it around the MCP handler. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_trace_test.go:356-422 (TestHostedToolCallsTracedPerRequest) checks three calls land in three traces, each a child of its POST /mcp span, with the attributes set. internal/observe/mcp_test.go:TestMCPMiddlewareSpanFromRequestHeaders covers the two-trace case.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:357 puts tel.MCPMiddleware outermost, ahead of a.MCPMiddleware (the rate limit). internal/hostauth/limit.go:110-118 returns the refusal as an IsError result, and allow(ctx) (limit.go:85-88) calls RecordContext with that ctx. observe/mcp.go:44-50 marks the span failed. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_trace_test.go:427-462 (TestHostedLimitedCallTraced) asserts the refused call has a failed span and that its limited record carries that trace and span ID.

internal/observe/board.go:14-36 BoardSpan starts a new root span "board <verb>" with tcgreplay.board.verb and tcgreplay.player, and links it to the live connection's span from ctx. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:326-332 sets webui.Server.Trace to it, and internal/webui/actions.go:90-103 calls it in dispatch for each action. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_trace_test.go:523-560 (TestHostedBoardActionsTraced) checks one trace per action, a root parent, and a single link to the GET /ws span.

internal/usergames/telemetry.go:59-72 writes the error record with RecordContext(ctx) and sets the span status to the same redacted message. internal/observe/sink.go:34-56 emits the record through the OTel logger with ctx, so it carries the span's trace and span IDs. observe/mcp.go:markFailed keeps that message. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_trace_test.go:468-518 (TestHostedFailedCallsMarkTheirSpans) checks the import error record's span ID matches the tools/call import_log span, that the trace matches, and that the span status message equals the record's message.

Most records comply: sign_in, sign_in_refused, limited, board_refused, sign_out and admin records use RecordContext with the request ctx (hostauth/google.go:94-95, 230; hostauth/board.go:134; usergames/board.go:31-34; hostauth/admin.go:41-52; cacheadmin/handler.go). Background records use plain Record. The gap is the account_removed record with reason "signed_out": usergames/usergames.go:159 (Release) calls r.cfg.Recorder.Record with no context. Release is reached on logout through hostauth/store.go:246-256 (releaseLocked -> onRelease), and the Places.Release(id string) interface (hostauth/hostauth.go:72) carries no ctx. So this sign-out-caused record carries no trace. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_trace_test.go:625-643 checks only the idle account_removed record and never the signed_out one. Fix: pass the request ctx into Release (or the release hook) and use RecordContext there.

With no Trace hook set, webui dispatch skips tracing (internal/webui/actions.go:90-103 checks s.Trace != nil; server.go:52-58 documents nil as the desktop). Telemetry without a sink calls Record with context.Background (internal/telemetry/recorder.go:127-185), so desktop records are unchanged. Desktop-side behaviour rests on the existing tests: internal/webui/trace_test.go:142 (TestNoTraceOnDesktop) and cmd/tcgreplay/desktop_telemetry_test.go. The go test run in the verify summary passed for all packages.

items.title: Image copies joined to their card request and the end-to-end privacy sweep

goal.title: Image copies joined to their card request and the end-to-end privacy sweep
criteria: A card request for an image with no copy yet shows the source fetch and the image store write inside its own trace, and the request itself does not wait for the copy.

In a scripted session (sign-in through to the first tool call, import, new game, board page, live connection, board action, card request, admin check), every HTTP request, tool call and board action appears as a span. None are missing.

Across everything the receiver got in that session plus a failed import of a log naming cards and players, there is no trace of the email, the Google tokens or code, the OAuth state, the board cookie or access token, the board handle, the client address or user agent, the battle log's text or the deck's card names. Players appear only as `p_…` IDs.
The static check fails if an email is passed to a span or log attribute.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/webui/server.go:244-256 calls s.Images.ImageContext(r.Context(), ...) on the card path. internal/cards/images.go ImageContext (diff ~2399-2418) only records the request's span context in spanCtx and queues the copy, so it returns without waiting. handle() (images.go:461-470) re-attaches that span context to the worker context before copyOne, so the source GET and store PUT run under the request's trace. internal/cards/images_trace_test.go:2491-2554 asserts the same trace ID for those four requests and that ImageContext returns within 50ms.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_telemetry_e2e_test.go:748-750 checks server spans against requestCounter, which counts only inbound requests that reach the playmat handler. Outgoing HTTP requests are not counted: the Google token/userinfo calls from the connector, the catalog loads and the Spaces listing. Client-span assertions are limited to the image PUT and the TCGdex GET inside the card trace (lines 767-783). Tool calls are counted (==3, lines 751-759) and board actions (==1, lines 760-762). The session's sign-in and outgoing calls therefore are not shown to produce a span for every HTTP request.

cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_telemetry_e2e_test.go:790-840 builds a secrets map (email, display name, Google access and ID tokens, client secret, playmat tokens, board cookie value, board handle, user agent, 'Go-http-client', 'code=', 'state=', 'board=', log player and opponent names, each log line, each deck card name, the malformed import line) and fails if any appears in h.r.Contains. goal.title: Usage counted as metrics
criteria: Each usage record increments exactly one matching counter with the right labels, and records that are not usage (for example game expiry) increment none.
Sign-ins carry `provider="google"`, and a sign-in record naming another provider carries that provider.
Assistants other than Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Gemini are counted as `other`, and tool names outside the registered tools as `other`.
Counters carry no player ID or other per-player label.

verdicts.evidence: internal/observe/metrics.go:53-77 (usage.count) maps each usage record to exactly one counter via a single switch: PlayerDay->player_days, SignIn->sign_ins{provider}, ToolCall->tool_calls{assistant,tool}, Import->imports{assistant}, NewGame->new_games{assistant}, Error->errors{kind}, Limited->limited{reason}. GameExpired, AccountRemoved, SignOut, SignInRefused, BoardRefused, AdminRefused and AdminAction fall through the switch and increment nothing. internal/observe/sink.go:59 calls s.usage.count once per emitted record. metrics_test.go:68-130 (TestUsageRecordsIncrementTheirCounter) checks the expected label sets and that the not-usage records produce no points.

internal/observe/labels.go:20-25 provider() returns "google" when the record names none and otherwise returns the named provider unchanged. internal/hostauth/google.go:233 records SignIn with Provider "google". metrics_test.go:75-78 checks provider=google for an explicit google record, the empty-provider record (counted as google), and provider=password and provider=github, which carry their own names.

The counters' attribute sets are built only in metrics.go:40-46 (no labels on player_days) and metrics.go:61-75 (provider, assistant, tool, kind, reason). A grep of all Go files under the code root for Int64Counter and attribute keys found no counter attribute named player or any per-player value; the only attribute "player" is in cmd/tcgreplay/noemail_test.go:149, which is a log attribute in a test. metrics.go:16-17 documents the closed-label rule and metrics_test.go:126-128 asserts no point carries a player label. items.title: Daily usage kept for six weeks with a dashboard

goal.title: Daily usage kept for six weeks with a dashboard
criteria: Against a fake metrics query API, the table read back is merged with newly finished days, repeated runs give the same table, and days older than six weeks are dropped.
When the query API is unreachable or rejects the request, the playmat keeps the table it has and keeps serving players. Failures count towards the five-minute warning.
The table is sent as one daily gauge series per day and count, with distinct players, sign-ins by provider, tool calls by assistant, imports, new games and errors.
Without the metrics query settings the usage history is off, the start-up line says so, and sending of everything else is unaffected.
The dashboard in the repository charts each count per day, and its queries name only metrics and labels the playmat sends.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/observe/history.go:142-193 (refresh) reads the table back with historyReadBack (line 51), merges by the larger value (155-157), computes only days with raw data that the table lacks (166-182, skipping via have[] and computeDay's historyPresent check at 198-206), and drops days before today-42 (184-191). internal/observe/history_test.go:204-332 TestHistoryRefreshMergesComputesAndDrops uses a fake query API (promFake, lines 36-134) and asserts the merged table, the 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12 cut-off, the 2026-11-19 zero-data skip, and that a second run gives the same table with only 11 queries and no recomputed day.

The run loop (history.go:266-280) ignores refresh errors, so serving is unaffected.

history.go:253-264 registers one Float64ObservableGauge tcgreplay.usage_daily; history.go:237-250 emits one point per table row with attributes day and count, plus provider or assistant only when set. The counts come from historyQueries (history.go:38-47): players, sign_ins by provider, tool_calls, imports and new_games by assistant, and errors. history_test.go:468-511 TestHistoryGaugeReportsEveryRow checks the exact point set.

internal/observe/settings.go:147-177 turns the history off with the reason 'no TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_METRICS_URL or TCGREPLAY_GRAFANA_METRICS_USER' when both are unset, and settings.go:179-204 Status() returns 'usage history: off (...)' into the start-up text. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:526-546 (hostedTelemetry) joins that with the export text; hosted.go:561 starts tel.Run. observe.go:157-165 creates history only when hs.on, and observe.go:189 runs it. observe.Start does not depend on the metrics settings for export. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_history_test.go:19-60 checks the start-up line says history is off and that the other data is still sent; lines 64-112 check the other states, and line 112 TestHostedSendsEverythingWithoutHistory covers the rest.

goal.title: Observability runbook rewritten for Grafana
criteria: The runbook no longer tells the maintainer to read records in Insights. It says platform metrics and alerts still come from App Platform.

It explains, step by step, how to read a day's distinct players and tool calls by assistant, find a player's error records from their email via the admin lookup, and open the trace of one of those errors and its other log lines.
It explains how to create the token (with the scopes needed), which settings to set where, how to import the dashboard and how to confirm sending from the start-up line.
It explains how to turn on Cloudflare Traces with the Grafana destination and forwarding to the origin, and where to record the reason if the edge part is unavailable.
Its Retention section states 14 days for records and traces, six weeks for daily totals and the platform metrics' figure, with sources and the date checked.
